title: Grove allocates across seven chains, including chains with little established track record
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.1.2 splits Grove's Active Instances by network before anything else: Ethereum Mainnet (.2.1), Avalanche (.2.2), Base (.2.3), Plasma (.2.4), Plume (.2.5), Monad (.2.6) and Robinhood Chain (.2.7).

The deployments outside Ethereum are deliberately thin and targeted rather than mirrored. Avalanche carries Centrifuge JTRSY and JAAA plus Curve USDS/USDC swaps and LP. Base carries two Morpho vaults. Plasma carries a single Aave v3 USDT0 position. Plume carries a single Centrifuge ACRDX position. Monad carries one Uniswap AUSD/USDC instance. Robinhood Chain carries a Morpho USDG vault and a Paxos conversion route.

Several of these are new or app-specific chains, and the pattern on each is the same: one or two positions, typically the same protocols Grove already uses on Ethereum. That is a **beachhead strategy** — establish presence with a familiar counterparty rather than a novel one, so the new variable is the chain alone.

Putting network at the top of the tree rather than protocol is what makes this legible. The same Centrifuge asset appears under both Ethereum Mainnet and Avalanche as **separate Instances with separate configuration documents**, so a chain-level problem can be reasoned about and unwound without touching the asset exposure elsewhere. Chain risk never gets collapsed into asset risk.
description: Beyond Ethereum Mainnet, Active Instances run on Avalanche, Base, Plasma, Plume, Monad and Robinhood Chain — each a separate directory branch, so chain risk is tracked independently of asset risk.
